{"decision": "APPLY", "workflow_yaml": "# This workflow will build a .NET project
# For more information see: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/automating-builds-and-tests/building-and-testing-net

name: Pull Request - Artifact Upload

on:
  pull_request:
    types:
      - opened
      - reopened
      - synchronize
    paths-ignore:
      - '**.md'

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: windows-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v7
      with:
        submodules: recursive

    - name: Cache NuGet packages
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.nuget/packages
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-${{ hashFiles('**/*.sln', '**/*.csproj', '**/packages.config') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-

    - name: setup-msbuild
      uses: microsoft/setup-msbuild@v3

    - name: Setup NuGet
      uses: NuGet/setup-nuget@v4

    - name: Restore Packages
      run: nuget restore ComicRack.sln

    - name: Build solution
      run: msbuild ComicRack\ComicRack.csproj -t:rebuild -property:Configuration=Release -property:Platform=AnyCPU

    - name: Upload artifacts
      id: upload
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
      with:
        name: "ComicRackCE_PR"
        path: "ComicRack/bin/Release/net48/*"
        if-no-files-found: error", "rationale": "The workflow runs `nuget restore` on every pull request, repeatedly fetching NuGet dependencies. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (dependency_cache mechanism) is supported by observational evidence reporting modest aggregate VM-time reduction from caching dependency downloads. Its preconditions are met: repeated dependency fetching is measurable (nuget restore executes each run), and cache inputs can be keyed to the solution/project/package manifest files as a proxy for a lockfile plus runner environment. Adding an actions/cache step before `nuget restore` preserves all build and test coverage unchanged—no step is removed, skipped, or altered—and introduces no new network access, secrets, privileged actions, or publishing/deployment operations. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT was considered but not applied because the repository CI history shows only failed runs, so the precondition of representative successful-duration history is not met and a safe timeout cannot be derived.", "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]}
